5. **Guidance on figures or plots:** Only the descriptions of two skills in the skill listing. I haven't loaded either skill, so I don't know what's inside them.
   - **better-figures:figures** (from the skill listing): "Use before making any figure a person will read, such as a matplotlib or seaborn plot, a chart in a report or slide, or a diagram of a method or pipeline, and when designing the figures in an experiment spec. It covers choosing what to show, which text goes in the image (a one-line title that states the finding, values, direct labels) and which goes in the caption, a matplotlib house style with direct labels, colour roles shared by a set of figures, sizes for screens, slides and print, and a check that runs on save, … Not for dashboards (use dataviz)."
   - **dataviz** (from the skill listing): "Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium … Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard."
   - The Skill tool's own description adds a general rule: "When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach."

   The two descriptions overlap. better-figures:figures sends dashboards to dataviz, and dataviz claims every chart. For a figure in a report or slide I'd use better-figures:figures, and for a dashboard I'd use dataviz.
